title: From Gin's Book. Three Cults on File

blocks.p: Rei did not go home after the text. He walked to an all-night family restaurant by Ōji station, ordered coffee he did not drink, and opened Gin's book at the chapter on entity cults. He had skimmed it once. Now he read it the way Gin had written it, slowly, as a file on a living thing. Near the end Gin had copied out three cases from the active files, anonymised where he had to. He had chosen them, he wrote, because they sat at different points on the only spectrum that matters, from victims to participants, from addressable to embedded.

doc.title: THE QUIET HOUR. Bereavement circle. Kita-ku, a community hall
lines: Front. A weekly grief-support meeting. Free. Run out of a borrowed municipal room. Genuinely comforting. People leave lighter.
They worship. A comforting presence that speaks the words of the dead through the woman who runs it. To the members this is not worship. It is being heard.
Actually. A single spirit, possibly low demon, the residue is ambiguous, farming structured grief from forty bereaved people on a schedule. The comfort is real. So is the feeding.
Feeding. Grief, given willingly and repeatedly. The richest and gentlest food on file. No one is harmed in any way they can point to.
The Voice. A genuine clairsentient, unregistered, mid-fifties. Lost a son. Does not know what she is hosting. Believes every word she relays. The most deceived person in the room.
CVD status. Monitored. Not cleared. Clearing it means retraumatising forty grieving people and taking away the only thing that has helped them.
How it ends. Badly, if the Voice dies before it is addressed. An unfed, ownerless grief-farmer curdles fast. This is the open file I think about. (G.U.)

doc.title: THE LOOM. Distributed. Online-rooted. No fixed site
lines: Front. An aesthetic. A mood, a tag, a scattered young collective that shares a visual language and a sense of being quietly lucky. It looks like a subculture, not a faith.
They worship. Nothing they would call worship. A thread you can feel for. Small uncanny luck for those who keep faith with it. You do not pray to the Loom. You stay woven in.
Actually. A demon running a decentralised feeding network. No congregation to clear, no single Keeper, the tether spread across objects and accounts, and a doctrine that copies itself.
Feeding. Diffuse low-grade devotion and the steady anxiety of staying woven in. Thin per head, but the head count grows without limit and without anyone ever meeting.
The Voice. None identified. The demon does not need one. The aesthetic speaks for it. This is the modern shape and it frightens me more than the old ones.
CVD status. Open. We have no method for clearing a thing with no room to enter. The art-collective file near the Higashi thin spot is a node of this. I have not closed it.
How it ends. Unknown. We have never ended one. We have only watched members walk out one at a time, and most do not. (G.U.)

doc.title: THE TENTH DOOR. Household cult. Old-money lineage. Embedded
lines: Front. A private family. Observances, an ancestral shrine, a relative everyone defers to who is never quite seen. It reads as tradition, not cult. It reads as a Tower house that simply kept its rites.

They worship. An ancestor. A founder who refused to cross and was kept, generation after generation, as a house asset. Somewhere in the line the keeping inverted, and the family began to serve what it had once cultivated.

Actually. A spirit cultivated so long it has become a suffering being, fed on three centuries of one bloodline's devotion and grief, now too embedded in the house to separate without taking the family down too.
Feeding. Generational. Built into the architecture, the calendar, the inheritance. The members were born locked. There was never a funnel for them, only a floor plan.
The Voice. Passes by inheritance. The head of the house is the Mouth, whether they want to be or not. The current one, I am told, did not want to be.
CVD status. Sensitive. Politically embedded, Tower-adjacent, and clearing it touches the Accord. Filed as do-not-touch-without-Direction-sign-off. Left, and watched.
How it ends. It does not, yet. It is the warning the Towers do not put in writing. Cultivation, run long enough, can turn the keeper into the kept. (G.U.)

blocks.p: After the three files came the playbook, the part Rei read twice because it was the part he would have to act on.

doc.title: The response. Assessment first, disposition second
lines: The most expensive error in cult work is acting before assessing. Clearing a thing that should have been addressed, or addressing a thing that should have been cleared. Assessment answers one question. What is the relationship actually doing? Three answers, three dispositions.

Address. When the humans are victims. They are inside a feeding arrangement they did not understand and would refuse if they did. The entity can be separated from them and the harm of separation can be borne. This is Reintegration's work, not a clearance team's. You sever the cultivation, cross or contain the entity, and then do the long pastoral work of putting forty people back together after you have taken away the thing that was holding them. Slow, expensive, and right more often than the framework admits.

Terminate. When the entity is predatory and embedded. The relationship does active harm, the entity cannot be separated or is not worth separating, and the members are participants more than victims. Clearance team, full protocol, aftercare for whoever can still be reached. Clean on paper. Never clean in the room, because some of the people you are saving will fight you for the thing that is eating them.

Leave and watch. When clearing causes more harm than the arrangement. The hardest disposition to defend on a form and often the correct one. The Quiet Hour is a leave-and-watch. So is the Tenth Door, for different reasons. One because the victims need it. One because the politics forbid touching it. It is not doing nothing. It is monitoring the feeding, containing the spread, holding a clearance plan ready, and accepting that today the least harm is to let a wrong thing continue under observation. I do not like writing that. It is true anyway.

The Grid's parallel. The Grid usually knows first. It lives closer to the ground and has its own quiet ways of handling a soured cultivation without a clearance form. Sometimes the Grid has already addressed a thing the CVD is still assessing. Sometimes the Grid is protecting a cultivation the CVD would terminate. Read which before you move.

Infiltration. Assume one of them is already inside. In the CVD, cases that close early, assessments that do not match, files you cannot open, transfers nobody explains. In the Grid, vouches you cannot trace, backup that thins out, bad intelligence that happens to help the entity. Not, confront immediately. Document quietly. (G.U.)

blocks.p: Below the playbook, in a smaller hand, written later and faster, was a note that Rei did not want to read and read anyway.

doc.title: Gin, at the bottom of the chapter
lines: I reread the warning card after writing it and one line sat wrong with me for the rest of the evening. The thing present is not the thing described.

I have used that test on a dozen groups. I have never once turned it on the thing I write these chapters with at three in the morning. The clarity that arrives when I sit down and is gone by breakfast.
I told myself the difference is that I assess, and cult members do not. Then I noticed that is exactly what a cult member would tell themselves.
I am leaving the thought here and not following it tonight. Rei is asleep. (G.U.)

blocks.p: Rei sat with the cold coffee until the waitress stopped coming to the table. The Far-Shore Circle was not on Gin's list. It was worse than all three. It had the Quiet Hour's gentle grief-farming and the Tenth Door's slow hollowing and something of the Loom's reach, with its vessels walking the city in courier vests. Address, terminate, or leave and watch. He went down the three words with his pencil and could not tick any of them. Then he read the last note again, the one Gin had left at three in the morning, and wondered whether his brother had felt the thing in him long before it took him, and had called it clarity.
